nodes.label: Circular economy in food systems

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Circular economy initiatives|Circular economy in food systems_qna_000
nodes.label: Strategy
nodes.question: What shift has occurred in sustainability science in recent years?
nodes.answer: There has been a shift toward greater emphasis on transformative change, requiring theories and methods that can address deeper, structural drivers of sustainability problems.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Circular economy initiatives|Circular economy in food systems_qna_001
nodes.label: Strategy
nodes.question: What is the main challenge addressed by food systems experts and organizations in 2023?
nodes.answer: The challenge of transforming the global food governance (GFG) system.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Circular economy initiatives|Circular economy in food systems_qna_002
nodes.label: Facts
nodes.question: How many global multi-stakeholder food system institutions (MIs) involving the ultra-processed food industry were identified in the study?
nodes.answer: The study identified 45 global food system MIs involving the ultra-processed food industry.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Circular economy initiatives|Circular economy in food systems_qna_003
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: What type of governance challenges does corporate-anchored multi-stakeholderism present for food systems transformation?
nodes.answer: It raises challenges for controlling and reducing ultra-processed foods in human diets.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Circular economy initiatives|Circular economy in food systems_qna_004
nodes.label: Facts
nodes.question: What crucial aspect is highlighted regarding the current global food system?
nodes.answer: It is unhealthy and unsustainable, necessitating urgent transformative change.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Circular economy initiatives|Circular economy in food systems_qna_005
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: What is the goal of transforming the global food governance system according to the paragraph?
nodes.answer: To overcome challenges related to the global food system.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Circular economy initiatives|Circular economy in food systems_qna_006
nodes.label: Strategy
nodes.question: What implications are discussed regarding UPF industry engaged multi-stakeholder governance?
nodes.answer: The implications discussed relate to food systems transformation and global responses to the health and environmental harms caused by UPFs.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Circular economy initiatives|Circular economy in food systems_qna_007
nodes.label: Factual
nodes.question: How can production and consumption be viewed in the context of the food system?
nodes.answer: Production and consumption should be understood as co-dependent parts of the food system that require cooperative efforts to achieve sustainability.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Circular economy initiatives|Circular economy in food systems_qna_008
nodes.label: Factual
nodes.question: What is necessary for successful regulatory instruments in promoting sustainable consumption?
nodes.answer: Successful regulatory instruments in promoting sustainable consumption must have ambitious, clear, and quantifiable targets to drive meaningful change in the food system.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Circular economy initiatives|Circular economy in food systems_qna_009
nodes.label: Strategy
nodes.question: What changes are called for in food production and consumption according to the paragraph?
nodes.answer: The paragraph calls for systemic and transformational changes towards a more sustainable paradigm in the way we produce and consume food, fibre, and fuel.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Circular economy initiatives|Circular economy in food systems_qna_010
nodes.label: Management
nodes.question: What role does responsible governance play in the transition to sustainable food systems?
nodes.answer: Responsible governance is highlighted as important for the transition to sustainable food, fiber, and fuel systems.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Circular economy initiatives|Circular economy in food systems_qna_011
nodes.label: Ethics and regulation
nodes.question: What two processes have contributed to the structure of modern food systems?
nodes.answer: Industrialisation and corporatisation have contributed to shaping modern food systems.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Circular economy initiatives|Circular economy in food systems_qna_012
nodes.label: Strategy
nodes.question: Which two interventions were piloted in the project?
nodes.answer: The two interventions aimed at reducing food waste and enhancing the protein transition.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Circular economy initiatives|Circular economy in food systems_qna_013
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: How is the model of capability and opportunity increasingly being used in relation to food and sustainability?
nodes.answer: The model of capability and opportunity is increasingly recommended and utilized as a tool to inform behavioural change strategies in relation to food and sustainability. It helps in understanding the interactions and barriers within each domain, enabling the development of effective strategies for promoting sustainable consumption and transitioning towards more plant-based diets.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Circular economy initiatives|Circular economy in food systems_qna_014
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: What were the findings regarding the association between Ultra-Processed Food (UPF) consumption and environmental impacts in Dutch adults?
nodes.answer: High UPF consumption was statistically significantly inversely associated with all environmental impact indicators, showing a decrease ranging from 13.6% to 3.0% when comparing the highest and lowest quartiles.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Circular economy initiatives|Circular economy in food systems_qna_015
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: What are some of the consequences of industrial processing of foods?
nodes.answer: Industrial processing of foods has increased the shelf life and availability of foods and beverages, leading to a decrease in hunger and undernutrition worldwide. However, it has also resulted in the exhaustion of natural resources and an increase in the production and consumption of ultraprocessed foods and drinks (UFDs).

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Circular economy initiatives|Circular economy in food systems_qna_016
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: How was a significant percentage of business food waste in Japan recycled in 2017?
nodes.answer: In Japan, 80% and 57% of the business food waste obtained from food manufacturing and wholesaling in 2017 were recycled into animal feed and fertilizer through policies like a certification system and mandatory heat treatment.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Circular economy initiatives|Circular economy in food systems_qna_017
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: What is the main focus of the book "System Innovation for Sustainability 1: Perspectives on Radical Changes to Sustainable Consumption and Production"?
nodes.answer: The main focus of the book is to explore radical changes needed for sustainable consumption and production.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Circular economy initiatives|Circular economy in food systems_qna_018
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: What is crucial for sustainable production and consumption (SPC) in the food industry, and why?
nodes.answer: Resource efficiency and waste minimization are essential for SPC in the food sector to promote economic sustainability and address ongoing issues like resource scarcity and climate change.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Circular economy initiatives|Circular economy in food systems_qna_019
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: How can digitalization and artificial intelligence contribute to the development of sustainable food systems?
nodes.answer: Digitalization and artificial intelligence can enhance the efficiency and effectiveness of sustainable food systems by optimizing processes, enabling better decision-making, and improving resource management to minimize waste and enhance sustainability.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Circular economy initiatives|Circular economy in food systems_qna_020
nodes.label: Management
nodes.question: How can organizations improve sustainable production and consumption while decreasing food loss and waste?
nodes.answer: Organizations can implement digital technologies and provide training and workshops to develop a skilled workforce for efficient implementation of digital technologies.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Circular economy initiatives|Circular economy in food systems_qna_021
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: How can multi-sector collaboration contribute to sustainable food waste recovery?
nodes.answer: Multi-sector collaboration can assist various food retail internet economies in making significant contributions to sustainable food waste recovery, reducing food waste, and achieving Sustainable Development Goals (SDG) targets.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Circular economy initiatives|Circular economy in food systems_qna_022
nodes.label: Management
nodes.question: How can systems of consumption and production be transformed to achieve the sustainable development goals, as discussed by Benson et al. (2018)?
nodes.answer: Benson et al. (2018) suggest moving beyond efficiency is necessary to transform systems of consumption and production for achieving the sustainable development goals.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Circular economy initiatives|Circular economy in food systems_qna_023
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: How can decreasing consumption of ultra-processed foods potentially improve environmental sustainability?
nodes.answer: Decreasing consumption of ultra-processed foods may reduce the environmental impact associated with food production and waste generation.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Circular economy initiatives|Circular economy in food systems_qna_024
nodes.label: Factual
nodes.question: Why is it important to understand the drivers of ultra-processed food production and consumption?
nodes.answer: Understanding the drivers helps in creating effective strategies to address the issues related to ultra-processed foods and their environmental impacts.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Circular economy initiatives|Circular economy in food systems_qna_025
nodes.label: Management
nodes.question: How can group model-building exercises help in conceptualizing the drivers of ultra-processed food production and consumption?
nodes.answer: Group model-building exercises can bring together diverse perspectives and expertise to identify and analyse the complex factors influencing the production and consumption of ultra-processed foods.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Circular economy initiatives|Circular economy in food systems_qna_026
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: What are some of the key global, regional, and national trends related to ultra-processed foods and the nutrition transition?
nodes.answer: Some key trends include the increasing consumption of ultra-processed foods, food system transformations, and the influence of political economy drivers on food choices and health outcomes.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Circular economy initiatives|Circular economy in food systems_qna_027
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: How are ultra-processed foods linked to food system sustainability?
nodes.answer: Ultra-processed foods are linked to food system sustainability through their impact on environmental resources, waste generation, and overall sustainability of food production.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Circular economy initiatives|Circular economy in food systems_qna_028
nodes.label: Facts
nodes.question: How have the food systems in Pacific Islands changed since decolonization, particularly regarding global food supply chains?
nodes.answer: Since decolonization, food systems in Pacific Islands have increasingly integrated into global industrialized food regimes, resulting in a shift from mostly local food sources to dependence on lower-quality imported foods, contributing to a rise in health issues like diabetes and obesity.
